# Dr. Allison Alimayu

> Dr. Allison Alimayu (formerly Allison Stephens) is a public interest futurist, keynote speaker, consultant, and board director based in North Carolina. The futures of children and families are decided in budgets, boardrooms, and evidence reviews, and she has worked in all three. Alimayu Studio is her intellectual atelier for research, policy, education, technology, faith, and impact.

## Identity
- Name: Dr. Allison Alimayu. Formerly Allison Stephens. Prior publications and public service records appear under Allison Stephens. Same person.
- Title: Public interest futurist.
- Education: PhD, Biomedical Informatics, Rutgers University (2020). Master of Education, Health Promotion, University of Nevada, Las Vegas (2004). Bachelor of Science, Health Care Administration, University of Nevada, Las Vegas (2002). Master of Science, Industrial and Systems Engineering, North Carolina A&T State University (in progress).

## Professional training
- Implementation Science Institute, University of Pennsylvania (2023)
- Pan-American Climate Resilient Health Systems, Columbia University (2023)
- Climate Change and Health, Yale University (2019)
- HOPE (Healthy Outcomes from Positive Experiences) Framework, Tufts Center for Community-Engaged Medicine (2021)
- Data Visualization, Depict Design Studio (2020)
- ArcGIS Geospatial Mapping and Analytics, University of California, Irvine (2018)
- LEAN for Process Improvement, Firefly Consulting and DaVita (2017)
- Health Ministry, Wesley Theological Seminary (2017)
- Political Campaigns Training, Emerge Nevada (2010)
- Health Economics, National Library of Medicine (2008)

## Record
- Nevada Board of Regents: elected November 2012; served January 2013 to January 2019; vice chair December 2016 to June 2017; chair, Audit and Compliance Committee.
- Medicare Evidence Development and Coverage Advisory Committee (MEDCAC): member, appointed by the US Secretary of Health and Human Services, 2019 to 2027.
- North Carolina Oil and Gas Commission: commissioner, appointed 2026.
- Fulbright US Scholar, Research Ireland, 2025 to 2026.
- Assistant professor, Department of Medicine, Tufts University School of Medicine, 2022 to 2024.
- UnitedHealthcare and UnitedHealth Networks, then DaVita Integrated Care, 2006 to 2018: designed a five-state value-based reimbursement program averaging $8.5 million in monthly savings.
- Campaigns: has run and won (Nevada Board of Regents, open seat, 2012). Consultant to local, state, and federal campaigns, including as a presidential campaign policy advisor. Candidate for US Congress, 2018.
- Democratic National Committee: elected member, two terms; secretary, Black Caucus; officer roles, Environmental and Climate Crisis Council.
- TEDx Carlow College, Ireland, 2026: "What is missing from science? The rest of us."
- Media: Fox News, CNN, CBS News, The Washington Post, The Guardian, The Hill, HuffPost, Nevada Public Radio, The Nevada Independent, Las Vegas Sun, KSNV, KLAS.

## Where she speaks
- Has spoken across the US, Ireland, and Europe, in person and virtually, with 200+ engagements including keynotes, commencement addresses, panels, trainings, podcasts, and live television.
- Available for in-person and virtual engagements across the Americas, from Canada to Latin America, and in Africa and Asia, including Kenya, Namibia, Indonesia, and Malaysia. Studied in Santiago, Chile.
- Formats: keynotes, panels, trainings, commencement addresses, podcasts, and media. Fees depend on format, travel, and audience size; nonprofit and public-sector rates are available.

## Speaking topics
Signature talks:
- Health systems and the business of care: how payment, coverage, and data decide who gets care, drawn from years inside UnitedHealthcare and DaVita and a federal seat on MEDCAC. Best for health plans, health systems, employers, and associations.
- Health policy, governance, and equity: how boards, budgets, and votes really work, from six years as an elected regent and service on state and federal bodies since 2010. Best for public agencies, boards, foundations, and civic and political events.
- What is missing from science? The rest of us: her TEDx talk, built out as a keynote on who gets a seat when evidence is weighed. Best for universities, research funders, and innovation conferences.

More topics, each available as a keynote, panel, or training:
- Climate and health: from an expert reviewer for the IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Cities and an officer of the DNC Environmental and Climate Crisis Council. Best for public health agencies, health systems, and climate and sustainability conferences.
- Child and family wellbeing: drawn from FAAITH and HOPE research with faith leaders and keynotes for infant mental health and afterschool networks. Best for child welfare, early childhood, education, and faith-based audiences.
- Running for office: from someone who has run and won, advised local, state, and federal campaigns, including as a presidential campaign policy advisor, and served as an elected member of the Democratic National Committee; pairs with the free masterclass Ballot ready. Best for candidate trainings, party and civic organizations, and leadership programs.
